4. **[Comparing Generative AI Tools - Research at Boston University](https://library.bu.edu/gen-ai/comparing-gen-ai-tools)**: It provides a comparison of popular AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude, detailing their features and pricing.

5. **[10 Best AI Tools for Business (November 2026) – Unite.AI](https://www.unite.ai/best-ai-tools-for-business)**: This article focuses on AI tools beneficial for business environments, including Microsoft 365 Copilot and HubSpot.

These resources should give you a comprehensive overview of the current AI tools available.

items.title: 11 Best AI Tools (2026): Ranked & Reviewed | Efficient App
items.summary:
Many AI tools have a free tier that lets you test the product before paying. Right now, I would absolutely use ChatGPT, Claude, Wispr Flow, Granola and Littlebird on their free plans. Perplexity and Gemini also have free tiers. These are some of the best free AI tools available right now for productivity, writing, research, note-taking, and everyday work. [...] But here's what most "best AI" lists don't tell you: the biggest productivity gains don't come from the chatbot itself. They come from AI tools that are built into the workflows you already use: AI agents, your email, meetings, etc. While ChatGPT and Claude are foundations, tools like Viktor AI, Granola AI, Superhuman Mail, Littlebird are really where the magic happens.

### What are the best free AI tools? [...] Start with ChatGPT if you're still new to AI tools. Add Claude if you work at a desk professionally, because Claude is better for long analysis, writing, and situations where you want the AI to ask clarifying questions before diving in. Use Gemini if your work already lives heavily inside Google Workspace.

### Where can I find honest AI tool reviews?

items.title: The 18+ Best AI Tools & Platforms 2026 (I Tested 30+)
items.summary:
For building software, Cursor, Replit, and Lovable serve different levels of technical experience. For marketing content across channels, Jasper keeps output consistent with a brand voice.

### 2. Which AI tools are free to use?

Several tools on this list offer free plans, including ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Perplexity, Granola, Wispr Flow, Notion, Replit, Cursor, Lovable, Gamma, ElevenLabs, Descript, Zapier, and Grok. [...] No. Tools such as Granola, Wispr Flow, Morgen, Gamma, Replit, Lovable, Microsoft Copilot, Zapier, Grok, and Jasper are all designed to be useful without much technical knowledge.

Cursor is aimed more directly at developers and people who already work with code.

### 5. Can AI tools integrate with my existing workflow?

Yes. Gemini works directly across Google Workspace, and Microsoft Copilot does the same across Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams. [...] There's no single best all-in-one solution; it depends on whether you need a generalist thinking tool or an assistant that can take action across your apps. Google Gemini and Claude are stronger for writing, research, and reasoning, while Zapier and n8n are stronger when the work involves integrations, repeated tasks, and real actions across your tools.

Creation

Agent Builder lets you “vibe code” agents, bringing them to production in minutes from just a prompt.

Capability

items.title: Comparing Generative AI Tools - Generative AI Tools for Students - Research at Boston University
items.summary:
ChatGPT

 Key Features: GPT-3.5 free; GPT-4 with browsing, data analysis, images
 Free Version: Yes
 Paid Version: Plus $20/month; Pro approximately $200/month

Claude

 Key Features: Long context, multiple styles, image input
 Free Version: Yes
 Paid Version: Pro $20/month; Max $100–200/month

Microsoft Copilot

 Key Features: GPT-4 integrated into Word, Excel, Outlook
 Free Version: Yes (available for BU accounts)
 Paid Version: Copilot Pro $20/month; 365 Copilot $30/user/month [...] Tip: Use grounded tools to surface leads and ideas, but don’t rely on them as your final source.

Examples: ChatGPT Plus (GPT-4), Perplexity AI, Copilot, Gemini.

##### 

##### Choosing the Right Tool

 Brainstorming & Drafting: ChatGPT, Claude
 Current Facts & Sources: Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot
 Summarizing Notes or PDFs: NotebookLM, Scite Assistant
 Idea to Topic: Generating Research Paper Topics with ChatGPT.

## Popular AI Tools: Features & Pricing

ChatGPT [...] + Exploring ideas
  + Summarizing documents
  + Locating potential sources

Tip: AI can accelerate research, but final verification and scholarly sources are essential.

##### Types of AI Tools

There are essentially two main types of AI tools: non-grounded and grounded.

Non-Grounded Tools

Definition: Models that rely only on their training data and do not access the live web.

Best for:

 Brainstorming ideas
 Drafting text
 Simplifying complex concepts

Things to watch for:

items.title: 10 Best AI Tools for Business (November 2026) – Unite.AI
items.summary:
Start with Microsoft 365 Copilot or Workspace with Gemini if the relevant information already lives in those suites. HubSpot is most useful with maintained CRM data, while Notion and monday.com benefit from well-organized workspace content.

### Compare broad assistants and delegated agents

ChatGPT and Claude are flexible tools for knowledge work. Symphony adds coordinated small-business agents. Zapier moves work across apps; Airia addresses enterprise AI control and governance. [...] | HubSpot Breeze and Agent Hub | AI for customer-facing HubSpot teams | Breeze Assistant and Agent Hub for marketing, prospecting, service, and data tasks |
| Microsoft 365 Copilot | AI in a Microsoft productivity environment | Work-connected chat and Copilot in Office and Teams apps |
| Symphony by Wix | Small businesses delegating work through conversation | One orchestrator, specialist and custom agents, connected tools, and approval checkpoints | [...] Business AI tools now cover much more than drafting and summarization. Assistants can work with documents and connected apps, productivity suites bring AI into daily work, and agents can carry out recurring processes. This guide compares those different roles so you can choose a useful addition to your existing systems rather than buy overlapping features under a broad AI label.
